claims.text: Increasing Al content in AlxCr0.2NbTiV to approximately x = 0.5 under controlled arc-melting and cooling conditions will produce a homogeneous single-phase BCC microstructure.
The resulting BCC microstructure will be solution-strengthened.
The x ≈ 0.5 alloy will rapidly form a stable alumina-rich passive film.
Lower-Al AlxCr0.2NbTiV variants exhibit mixed-phase regions.
Lower-Al variants have only moderate strength, creep resistance, and corrosion protection.
A controlled atmosphere and uniform cooling rate will help achieve a homogeneous single-phase BCC structure.
Increasing Al content raises the dislocation activation energy under ambient conditions.
The increased dislocation activation energy will reduce room-temperature creep.
Elevated Al content promotes formation of a protective alumina-rich passive film.
The alumina-rich passive film improves corrosion resistance.
Relative to the lower-Al or as-cast baseline, the x ≈ 0.5 alloy will have higher yield strength.
Relative to the lower-Al or as-cast baseline, the x ≈ 0.5 alloy will have higher ultimate tensile strength.
Relative to the lower-Al or as-cast baseline, the x ≈ 0.5 alloy will have a lower room-temperature creep rate.
Relative to the baseline, the x ≈ 0.5 alloy will have a lower corrosion current density.
Relative to the baseline, the x ≈ 0.5 alloy will have a higher pitting potential during salt-solution testing.
The proposed improvements should persist at ambient and moderately elevated service temperatures typical of aerospace fasteners.
Al content beyond the optimal range may promote brittle intermetallic phases and eliminate the desired property improvements.
The improvements should be significant enough to meet aerospace fastener standards.
